overall: Tomorrow (Friday, June 26) is expected to be partly sunny and warm, with a 40% chance of afternoon showers and thunderstorms developing after 1pm per NWS guidance. Conditions will be notably more active than today, though afternoon convection could act as a temperature cap. Active flood warnings are in effect for the Satilla River corridor in southeastern Georgia (Ware, Pierce, and Brantley counties), which reflects ongoing moisture in the region but has no direct bearing on Atlanta's max temperature.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show meaningful spread: ECMWF is the clear warm outlier at ~90.3°F, while GFS (~84.5°F) and Weather.com (~84.2°F) are the coldest, with NBM (~87.0°F) and HRRR (~86.5°F) splitting the middle. max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble (incorporating today's anomalously cool 75.2°F observed high) yields an expected TMAX of 83.2°F, while the forecast-only model gives 86.7°F and the NWS targets near 90°F. Given today's large miss on the warm side, the obs-inclusive ensemble estimate deserves more weight, though the ECMWF's strong 90-91°F signal and Friday's partly sunny sky keep the warm tail alive. The distribution is broad and fairly flat from 80°F through 93°F, with the top probability bucket at 90-91°F (23.2%) and substantial mass in the mid-80s, reflecting genuine uncertainty; confidence is moderate at best (Tier 2).
